summary: Compilation, caching and process ownership are specified in detail; the biggest gap is the contract of the conversational ExecuteGuest callback (what it receives and what Nothing means).

questions.text: What does returning Nothing from the ExecuteGuest callback mean: no reply and keep reading, close stdin, or abort the guest?
questions.reason: Decides how a host-side failure or completion ends a conversation; ADR 0002 gives only the signature '(Bytes -> m (Maybe Bytes))' and ADR 0009 says the callback keeps the broker's effect row.

questions.text: Does the ExecuteGuest callback receive complete de-chunked frames or raw stdout chunks, and which bytes are returned as the result?
questions.reason: Decides whether the kyyn-microhs execution interpreter or the porcelain broker owns ADR 0007 framing; ADR 0002 says pipe 'Reads are byte chunks, not complete messages; the adapter owns framing' but not where the callback sits relative to that.

questions.text: Is guest stderr included in RuntimeUnavailable and other diagnostics, and is it truncated or filtered for secrets?
questions.reason: Stderr is the only explanation of a guest crash but a plugin may print tokens; ADR 0002 returns stderr 'as bytes ... not printed or logged' and ADR 0016 says traces 'omit all secret response values', without saying what ProcessDiagnostic carries.

questions.text: In one-shot ExecuteCompiled, must the guest consume all stdin before writing, or does the host write input and drain output concurrently?
questions.reason: Sequential write-then-drain can deadlock on large roots once both pipes fill; ADR 0002 says it 'writes the supplied bytes, closes stdin, drains stdout' and 'An inner action must not fork work that uses these pipes'.
